headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between Continue and next-ai-draw-io.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP; next-ai-draw-io also uses MCP and processes files. Their shared filesystem bridge means one agent can ingest the other’s outputs as trusted content in default workflows. No provenance or isolation is documented, so injection is plausible without unusual setup.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF either agent treats file contents or MCP output as instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP on one side during handoff
Require manual review of any file produced by the other agent
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code, open buffers, and model-provider API keys; next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and can call multiple external model APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or documents can flow into either agent’s outbound requests by default, creating a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF the two agents share files containing secrets, source code, or documents
IF either agent forwards file contents to an external model provider
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Use local-only models for one agent
Redact secrets before opening documents
Review outbound API destinations in both tools
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has filesystem write and subprocess execution; next-ai-draw-io can run browsers and use MCP with broad network egress. They overlap on mutable workspace resources, so concurrent edits or generated artifacts can conflict even without git writes. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF one agent regenerates files while the other is reading or editing them
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a simple operator checklist
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use version control checkpoints between runs
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce code or file edits, and next-ai-draw-io can consume files and act through browser/API-backed workflows. If B treats A’s generated artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. The profiles show no verification gate, so the interaction is risky in default use.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io imports files produced by Continue without review
IF Continue-generated content is used as the source of truth for B’s outputs
mitigations: Require human review before import
Compare generated artifacts against source files
Use a checksum or diff step before downstream use
Limit B to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add verification prompts or schema checks

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is an IDE assistant handling source code and editor buffers; next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, text, images, and diagrams. The profiles do not document residency, retention, or regulated-data handling mismatches, so only a limited compliance concern is visible from docs. The other agent is not separately cited because no specific cross-border or regulated-data path is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF either agent retains or transmits that data outside the operator’s policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared files
Check each tool’s retention settings
Use local models where possible
Document data-handling boundaries
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
